To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of water quality models depends on the dynamic of pollutograph and the predictive capacity of models depends on the time scale considered.

the performance of water quality models depends on the type of event (first flush or non first flush) and the time scale (short-term or long-term) and that the wash-off model performs better than the build-up models on short periods and the intra-event data assimilation approach performs better for first flush events on short periods.

the performance of build-up and washoff models is related to the dynamics of pollutant transport and that the predictive capacity of the washoff model is better for short periods and that the build-up model based on antecedent dry period cannot predict satisfactorilly the accumulated mass on surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the performance and the predictive capacity of the most common models on different temporal scales.
the development of a methodology to evaluate and compare the performance of water quality models on different temporal scales.
the evaluation of the performance and predictive capacity of the build-up and the wash-off processes in order to provide an efficient stormwater management tool for urban catchment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of water quality models is highly dependent on the type of model and on the type of events.
the wash-off approach is more suitable for short-term prediction while the build-up approach is more suitable to simulate the pollutograph and predict long-term pollutant accumulation.
the wash-off models are more appropriate to simulate the short-term behavior of suspended solids in runoff, while build-up models are more appropriate for the long-term behavior of the pollutant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wash-off model can be used as a first approximation for the simulation of pollutographs, while the build-up model should be used to predict the total accumulated mass.
the models are able to predict the pollutant transport for the first flush events but not for the rest of the storm.
the models have different capacities to simulate and predict the pollutograph depending on the temporal scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the model and the parameterization of its input variables are crucial for the accurate representation of pollutograph.
the wash-off process seems to be the best approach for modeling the temporal variability of pollutant concentrations in runoff.
the choice of a model should be based on the specific objectives of the study and on the type of event.
